title: Controls the priority of conflicting styles
goal: Use a selector with a higher priority so that the color of the specified state can take effect even if it is written first.
summary: When rules in the same common style sheet set an attribute at the same time, the browser will first compare the selector priorities. If the priorities are the same, the rule written later will take effect.
tasks: only edit style.css, add rules in the comments, and change the text of "delivery delayed" to #9a3412.
Make new rules #delivery-alert before existing rules. Keep the original rules so that "delivery is normal" continues to appear green.
hint: Make new selectors match both existing IDs and classes. Only writing the same ID will have the same priority as subsequent rules.

example.note: has id="credits" and class="footer-note". The first rule matches one more class, has a higher priority, and brown takes effect.
